comments.subject: Public Comments Form
comments.comment:
To whom it may concern,

This is a story in our neighborhood that involves failures by large businesses (Quality Excavation and Salisbury) and the city of St. George, leaving the homeowners in a difficult position. The city of St. George says it's not their responsibility. (Why do they require plans, approvals and inspections?) Salisbury is hiding behind arbitration clauses. Quality Excavation doesn't want to admit they missed completing the project as it was approved. If any of these entities had done their job, this problem wouldn't exist. Who will step up and do the right thing and resolve the problem?

The problem is a drainage and flooding problem. When we get the typical St. George rain storms, we all have to deal with the back yards flooding and threatening our homes. The above named entities failed to do their job to install a 10 inch drain pipe system across the back yards of the six lots involved. We should have a passive drainage system, but instead, we are having to install and maintain sump pumps. The city even told me it was my responsibility to get the permission to put the drainage through the below neighbor's yard. This causes undue expenses and stress on the homeowners for something that was missed being done according to the approved plans. There were lots being changed from walkout basement lots to slab on grade, that should have required drainage plans and other approvals to be done, but those were never done. Six building permits were issued by the city with this drainage system missing.

I included screen shots of documents in the attached document to make it easier to read, but I have gathered, and willing to share, all the documents related to this problem and these lots.

What can a homeowner do when companies fail to do their job? What does the homeowner do when it's a government entity, tasked with approving plans and verifying the work was completed as approved, fails to do their job? What is the point of having a process for permits and approvals if those rules aren't followed or enforced? What role are the mayor and city council playing in this process? Do the rules only apply to everyone else and not for a select few? Who failed to do their job? Maybe the city should pull permits and issue stop work orders for the businesses who don't follow the rules or take care of their customers.

Please review the attached document and let me know if you have any questions or want more information. I look forward to getting this resolved.

Thank you,
Jeremy Cluff

File Upload: Desert Rim Drainage Failures_compressed.pdf
